name: Darren W. Woods

career.title: Planning analyst, then domestic and international roles
Director of Refining, Europe, Africa and Middle East (Brussels), then Vice President of Supply and Transportation
President; Vice President of Exxon Mobil Corporation

background_rationale: An electrical engineer by training who rose through Exxon's chemicals, refining and supply businesses before leading the company.

notable.summary: Exxon lost a proxy fight to activist investor Engine No. 1, which won three seats on the company's board after campaigning over its climate and capital-spending strategy.
ExxonMobil completed its roughly $60 billion all-stock acquisition of Pioneer Natural Resources, more than doubling its Permian Basin production.
Woods said the incoming Trump administration should keep the United States in the Paris climate agreement.
ExxonMobil announced it would cut about 2,000 jobs globally as part of a restructuring plan.

personal_story.hook: At 16, Darren Woods unloaded overseas containers at a Navy warehouse in Hawaii; he now runs ExxonMobil.
personal_story.summary: Woods was born in Wichita, Kansas, in 1965, and because of his father's work as a military supplier he spent much of his youth near U.S. military bases around the world. At 16 he worked at a Navy warehouse in Hawaii unloading overseas containers, which he has described as hard, hot and very dirty work alongside people from different backgrounds. He studied electrical engineering at Texas A&M University and later earned an MBA from Northwestern's Kellogg School of Management. He joined Exxon in 1992 as a planning analyst in New Jersey and, moving roughly every three years across the U.S., Europe and Asia, rose through chemicals and refining to become chairman and CEO in 2017.
